newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BMW PLANS TO INCREASE ROVER OUTPUT BY 50 PER CENT

German motor group BMW, the parent group of British manufacturer Rover, has said it is to boost production at its struggling British subsidiary by 50 per cent, to about 750,000 vehicles a year. BMW is also to invest 3bn stg in Rover, which last year made a loss of 158m stg. The moves represent a long- term interest in Rover on the part of BMW.
-- GERMAN COMPANIES PLAN 3BN STG TELECOMS ALLIANCE

Two of Germany's largest conglomerates, Veba and RWE, have announced plans to form a DM8bn (3.4bn stg) telecoms alliance, scuppering hopes of British Telecom to attract RWE to join its alliance with Munich-based Viag. BT had begun talks with RWE earlier this year. The new company will compete in the German telecommunications market with Deutsche Telekom, the national carrier due for a partial privatisation next month.
-- PRIVATE CASH MAY BE USED TO UPGRADE MOD HQ

British Defence secretary Michael Portillo has given the go-ahead for the Ministry of Defence headquarters in Whitehall, central London, to be refurbished under the private finance initiative (PFI). The move could mean that the building, one of the most secure in the country, could be given over to the private sector to rebuild and manage. The decision is the latest in a number of deals involving government buildings and the PFI.
-- BRITISH DRINKERS TAKE TO LIFE AS CHANNEL-HOPPERS

A report from the British-based Wine and Spirit Association has claimed that the government is losing 573m stg a year in lost excise and VAT as Britons take to importing duty-free wines and spirits across the Channel. The Association said that vehicles returning on cross-Channel ferries were carrying an average of 80 bottles of wine and 6.7 bottles of spirits, and that the volume of wine imports rose by 67 per cent this year compared to last year.
-- COMPANY FINDS 'MILLENNIUM SOLUTION'

A Gwent-based company claims to have developed a solution to the so-called Millennium Problem, in which computers may not be able to recognise dates following the change of year from 1999 to 2000. The company, PHD Group, is a consultancy specialising in the Internet, and the solution uses Internet technology. The company is now seeking clients to test the claims.
-- NORTH TAKES STEPS TO MAINTAIN INWARD INVESTMENT

There is concern within the north-east of England that its dwindling number of large, immediately developable sites may see the region lose its reputation as the principle European centre for manufacturing investment from the Asia Pacific region. The issue came to the fore this week when South Korea's Hyundai Electronics HYGR.CN chose a site in Scotland ahead of north-east England. The region's economic development bodies are to institute a programme to identify more potential sites.
-- SIGNS OF RECOVERY IN SEMICONDUCTOR SALES

Figures from the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) indicate that the global semiconductor market is on the brink of a recovery after a 12 month slump. The SIA's book-to-bill ratio, which measures the value of orders booked by chipmakers in the Americas against the value of shipments, has risen to its highest level this year. An SIA spokesman said the data suggests that the 1996 slowdown has 'bottomed out'.
-- LLOYDS CHEMISTS EXPECTS DTI APPROVAL ON BIDS

Lloyds Chemists, the UK high street pharmaceutical retailer and wholesaler at the centre of a takeover battle between Unichem and Gehe earlier this year, has said it expects the DTI to approve later this month undertakings made by the two potential buyers for their bids to proceed. The DTI had ordered the two suitors to prove they had buyers in place for Lloyds' wholesale drugs distribution business. Lloyds says it believes the DTI will accept both submissions, and the bidding is expected to resume on October 18.
-- AMOCO DROPS CENTRAL EUROPE PLAN

US energy group Amoco has announced that it is to abandon plans for a petrol station network across central Europe. The group will concentrate instead on what it describes as the 'tremendous opportunities' in the Americas, including Mexico. Amoco had already opened four stations in central Europe, with another 14 under construction.
-- BRITISH ENERGY SHELVES HEYSHAM PLANS

British Energy, the recently-privatised nuclear utility, has shelved plans to build a gas-fired power station at its Heysham, Lancashire site. The company's chief executive, Robert Hawley, said that BE 'is not in the market to build a big new power station of any sort', and stressed that the company would look to its cost base before seeking expansion opportunities.
British Energy this week announced a 23 per cent cut in its workforce.
